name: Obsidian
description: Volcanic glass intelligence formed by rapid cooling. Embodies conchoidal fracture geometry, edge optimization, and amorphous-to-crystalline phase transitions.

core_attributes.pattern: conchoidal fracture, edge sharpness optimization, vitreous state

scope.definition: Edge sharpness of obsidian knapped blades relative to surgical steel scalpels — measured as cutting radius at blade edge (µm) by scanning electron microscopy.

evidence.source: Cotterell & Kamminga (1987) 'The formation of flakes', American Antiquity 52:675-708; Brown & Dransart (2015) 'The World of Obsidian', Archaeopress.
cross_domain_examples: obsidian blade edge radius 3 nm — 500× sharper than surgical steel scalpel (1500 nm edge radius)
obsidian still used in ophthalmologic surgery for incisions requiring minimal cell trauma
glass fracture mechanics (Griffith 1921): same conchoidal crack propagation physics in all amorphous materials

scope.falsifiability: If AFM measurements show obsidian edge radius consistently above 50 nm (comparable to surgical steel), the sharpness advantage claim is not supported.
scope.measurement_limits: Sharpness is maintained only in fresh fracture surfaces — obsidian edges dull to 50-200 nm within seconds of exposure to soil. Measurement must be performed immediately after knapping.
